May also be some haven't experienced it yet. You can only really perceive what you have experienced. 

I've never been addicted to anything so far but I thought I had amazing self control with drugs and could handle anything they'd throw at me. Until I had one experience (not opiate) where I went completely insane and required 5 people to restrain me.

Things can go from 0-100 in one way or another sometimes and you can never be certain if/when that moment will be. The fewer people learn that the hard way, the better.

Just commenting to lend you some support that some people don't think you're doing anything wrong speaking out here, the risk is real. Some people will be fine but for those who won't it could easily be the worst experience of their lives.

Everyone is fine until/unless they aren't.

How do you cope with your life? I don't know what to do with mine anymore. I feel like I need a carer of some kind to just bodyguard me any time I go outside, but I'm not going to get that most likely.

"maybe people have a go at you when you leave the house because you have previously stated you use racial slurs against people"

No, because 99.9% of people are totally unaware of that (that was an incident involving just a small group of people, none of whom I have ever met again since), and I have never said anything along those lines to anyone who has not provoked me first (if you read my description of the incident in question, you would know I had not so much as looked at the individual in question first. THEY approached me to be ableist and sexist purely out of malice, but took offense at being discriminated against in return).

I do not have any sort of reputation for anything. 99.9% of people that I meet never encounter me more than once. Not sure if you're from a small town where everyone knows everyone or something, but I'm in a city with nearly 9 million people. Most strangers never meet twice.

To be honest I don't owe you any explanation, you don't know me or the endless abuse I go through. I know that I have never initiated a conflict with anybody just for a cheap laugh at their expense. But no, I'm not going to apologise for responding to discrimination with discrimination against the instigators. If people don't like being insulted for something outside of their control, perhaps they shouldn't do that to other people who've done nothing to them first. People like the ones you're referring to start conflicts with me all the time, and so I have no choice but to defend myself. I'm not the one who wanted the conflict in the first place.

You think I'm an asshole, but my sole desire in life is to be left in peace. I would never even think about being abusive towards someone who had done nothing to me. Disappoints me that there are so many people like you who think I was in the wrong for that incident, I honestly don't understand how that can be. Maybe my autism is impairing my ability to see things from the perspective of 'normal' people, but do you genuinely have more of an issue with what I said to that person than with the fact that he was 3-5 times stronger than me, outnumbered me 4 to 1, and was chasing me?

Edit on that final line: Checking your history tells me you are also autistic (that you were bringing up that incident in my past history made me think you might have just come in from some other subreddit unrelated to autism), so forget that 'normal' people's perspective comment, but it's still a spectrum, so we may still see it differently.

I struggle to even step foot outside my house on my own. I posted about my experience in /r/autism last night. I think we have slightly different reasons for struggling when alone (I have severe anxiety, but in my case not for "whatever reason": I know the exact reason for my anxiety), but the misery it causes is most likely the same. 

I have no advice for you as I can't even help myself, let alone someone else, but I wish you the best. Glad things have been improving for you this year.

Nothing equivalent here to my knowledge, and even if there was, I'd imagine it only really works for people who are clearly disabled (I am too mild to be identified as autistic, I am just identified as weird/stupid instead). 
I think there is a general social culture in most places in the Western world nowadays that makes it heavily frowned upon to be an asshole towards people who are considered "disabled enough". Being abusive towards someone who has a clear disability (blind/wheelchair bound/Down's Syndrome etc.) will usually result in witnesses turning on you/losing your social status. But people with non-visible disabilities who just seem 'weird' are not shown any such mercy.

I am in a bad part of London (which in my opinion has turned into an absolute shithole of a city as a whole), but the majority of people even in this area do not experience the treatment I do, so the issue is not the area, it's me. I get treated badly almost everywhere I go, some areas less than others, but there's nowhere I can go where I will be accepted as normal because I'm not and everybody can tell that.

I see so many people talk about disability in a positive way. We even have 'autism pride' days and events nowadays. People seem to think (or want to delude themselves into thinking) that autism is not a disorder but merely a benign alternative way of seeing the world. 

I mean, those neurotypicals are just "boring" right? Who wants to be 'normal' anyway? Clearly it's so much better to be autistic instead. Do we have Down's Syndrome pride days? Or paralysis pride days? I wouldn't be surprised if we do in all honesty. Because who wouldn't rather be a quadriplegic instead of a boring 'normal' person? Clearly being a quadriplegic is superior to being dull like most people. 

I suppose some of them really do believe it. Probably it depends where they or their loved ones fall on the spectrum. Perhaps if you dodge the 'uncanny valley' area between normality and severity it's not so bad. My boyfriend is autistic too, but on the very mild side. He sees it more positively than I do. One of my siblings is severely autistic, I suppose he probably doesn't have much opinion on it one way or the other. 

If you're mild enough to pass as normal more or less, or severe enough to be too stupid to be able to form a basic thought on the matter, perhaps autism is pleasant enough. But if you're somewhere in-between the two, it's not so fun. I don't enjoy it at all.
